title: Tenant-anchored Observability Eraser and Access Ledger
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Background: As Redwood grows its multi-tenant footprint, on-call and analytics workflows increasingly need tenant-scoped controls for observability data. Current retention and redaction are coarse-grained: logs and traces are retained by pipeline-level TTLs and a handful of scrubbers. This task builds a tenant-anchored erasure pipeline plus an immutable access ledger to meet compliance requests and improve dev/debug ergonomics without destabilizing runtime pipelines.

Scope: Implement tenant-scoped 'eraser' markers and an access ledger for observability streams (traces, logs, metrics metadata) such that: (1) PII-containing spans and log entries can be identified and evicted on request, (2) redaction decisions propagate through downstream storage (cold and hot) and derived metrics, and (3) all manual/automated access or erasure actions are recorded with tenant-scoped audit entries. This ticket covers design, pipeline adapters, a minimal console surface for requests, and a tracing hook for span provenance tagging.

Non-goals: Full UI for self-serve deletion across all console surfaces (will follow), reingestion workflows for all historical metrics (out of scope), and cross-tenant trace reconstruction for debugging (privacy constraint).
acceptance_criteria: Tracing SDK: spans can be annotated with tenant_id and pii_markers at ingestion time and preserved through our sampling/batching layers

Eraser pipeline: given a tenant erasure request (tenant_id + predicate), matching entries in hot storage and cold copy are either redacted or tombstoned within SLA (48h for cold lane) with a verification report
Access ledger: every access or erasure action emits an immutable ledger entry written to an append-only store accessible to security for audits
RBAC controls: only allowed roles can initiate erasure or view ledger entries; console surface enforces role checks
No increase in p95 generation latency by >5% for requests when tracing hooks are enabled (baseline measured)
technical_notes: Instrumentation: add lightweight span tags: tenant.id, pii.score (0-1), pii.schema_tags (comma-separated). Propagate through the continuous-batching layer as metadata; do not inject into tokenized payloads.
Eraser markers: implement an eraser-index that stores tombstone predicates (tenant_id + field paths + time-range) and a versioned marker to coordinate cross-pipeline purge jobs.

Pipeline adapters: introduce a 'retention adapter' to kafka->ingest that checks eraser-index and applies redaction transforms before sink to hot index; cold exports get a signed purge manifest for async deletion.

Access ledger: ledger entries are JSONL lines with fields (timestamp, actor, tenant_id, action, query_hash, outcome) signed with service key; write to a separate cluster with 7-year retention and read-API for security.
Just-in-time debug: support rehydration tokens for on-call that return a time-limited, audited view of redacted data for debugging; requires explicit approval flow in console
Quality: use deterministic pseudonymization for metric labels (HMAC with tenant key) to keep metric cardinality low while preserving diagnostic correlation when allowed by policy

2025-01-18 Priya Kaur (Security): Requirement: access ledger must be append-only and signed. Need KMS integration and HSM key usage for signature keys. Raised security_review_required.
2025-01-22 Design review: agreed on console UX with 2-step confirmation and export of verification report. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OBS/Eraser+UX

2025-01-28 Engineering note: batch-layer changes landed in branch feature/eraser-prop (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5342). Observed +3% p95 in local microbenchmark; optimizing metadata copying to cut overhead.

2025-02-02 QA: First end-to-end run against canary ingestion cluster. Hot deletes applied; cold purge manifests generated. Minor bug: ledger write retried on transient 503, added exponential backoff and dead-letter alert.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: inadvertent data loss if predicate too broad. Mitigation: require human approval for any erasure covering >1,000 rows or >30 days; provide verification snapshot before finalization.
Risk: increased tail latency due to added metadata propagation. Mitigation: make tracing tags optional flag per route and ensure propagation happens off-thread where possible.
Risk: ledger storage cost. Mitigation: compress ledger entries and partition by month; provide retention lifecycle for internal-case-only entries.
Risk: metric cardinality explosion from pseudonyms. Mitigation: HMAC-based bucketing and cardinality cap enforcement in metrics pipeline.
